rooms.1000: The valley road ends at a broad marble landing where the White Marble Stairs begin their long climb. Pale steps rise overhead into a shaft of cold light, each one worn hollow in the middle by ages of divine feet. Tall columns frame the opening onto the valley, and the way back runs west to the valley floor. Thunder rolls somewhere high above, and the air smells faintly of honey.
rooms.1053: The valley floor is paved here with cracked white flags, and the great stairs stand close by to the east, pale against the mountain. Wind carries a hint of ambrosia down from the heights. The path bends south along a dry watercourse filled with fallen marble blocks. Thunder mutters from clouds that never quite leave the peaks.
rooms.1052: Three ways cross in the long shadow of the mountain, where scree and pale grass crowd the broken paving. The path runs north toward the foot of the great stairs, south into a hollow of the valley, and west along the slope. A shattered plinth stands in the middle of the crossing, its figure long gone.
rooms.1054: The valley narrows into a blind hollow walled by sheer grey rock streaked with white veins of marble. Nothing grows here but wiry thistles, and the only way out is the path back north. An old altar slab, split down the middle by lightning, lies half buried in the gravel. The air is still and warm and tastes of dust and honey.
rooms.1051: Banks of wild thyme grow between toppled columns here, and the heat hums with bees. The path leads east toward a crossing and turns south down a gentle slope of loose stone. High above, the peak is hidden in a crown of storm cloud lit from within by pale flashes.
rooms.1050: A long shelf of bare rock carries the path, with a fall of loose scree on one hand and the mountain wall on the other. Lightning-scarred pines cling to cracks in the stone. The path runs north to a patch of thyme and west toward a larger meeting of ways. A line of weathered marble milestones, carved with letters no one reads now, marks the edge of the drop.
rooms.1048: Three paths meet where a stream once ran, its bed now a ribbon of white pebbles. To the north the way climbs gently toward the valley mouth, to the east it follows a rocky shelf, and to the south it drops toward a roofed crossing of tall pillars. A thin keening cry echoes off the cliffs and dies away.
rooms.1046: Pale dust lies deep on the valley road, rutted by the wheels of chariots from some forgotten procession. The road runs north toward the valley's mouth and south to a junction of paths, while a narrow track bends west into a small side hollow. Poppies grow thick in the ditches, startlingly red against the white stone.
rooms.1045: The valley opens wide here, ringed by cliffs of gleaming white rock that catch every flicker of the storm. The road runs north toward the valley's mouth and south deeper into the high basin. Broken paving stones show where a grander avenue once ran, and a lone cypress leans over the verge.
rooms.1044: The old road climbs out of the foothills here and passes between two weathered marble pillars into the Great Valley. Back to the north the road runs open and clear down toward the Great Forest of MiNar, whose dark canopy shows faintly through the haze. South of the pillars the valley lies spread out, pale and enormous beneath a bruised sky. A carved lintel across the pillars is cracked by frost.
rooms.1047: A small hollow opens off the valley road, floored with cracked mosaic tiles whose pictures have faded to ghosts of blue and gold. A dry fountain basin sits in the middle with a stone spout worn smooth. The only way out is back east to the road. The wind makes a low humming among the broken tiles.
rooms.1049: Four marble porticoes meet beneath a single great domed roof held up by a ring of fluted columns. Daylight falls through a round opening in the dome onto a star inlaid in gold and black stone. Archways lead north toward the pebbly stream bed, east into a small court, south along a colonnade and west to a steep track. Faint thunder shakes dust from the cornice.
rooms.1055: A small walled court lies off the pillared crossing, paved in squares of rose and white marble and overgrown with creeping vines. A stone bench faces a mural of cloud-borne chariots, flaking away in great patches. The only way out is back west under the domed roof. The scent of old ambrosia hangs in the still air, thick and sweet.
rooms.1056: A colonnade runs along the foot of the cliff, its columns leaning at odd angles from the tremors of ages. To the north it ends at the domed crossing, to the east a stony path winds off along the valley floor, and to the south the colonnade falls away into a narrow gully. Grey cloud slides across the peaks. A fallen capital carved with acanthus leaves lies in the way.
rooms.1059: The path squeezes between two shoulders of pale rock that gleam like wet bone. Water seeps down the cliff and gathers in a clear pool beside the track. West lies the leaning colonnade, and east the path continues past a spill of boulders. Thunder echoes in the narrow place like a drum.
rooms.1060: A bend in the valley wall opens a wider view of the high basin, with silver threads of waterfall far off on the cliffs. The path turns north up a stony rise and west back toward the pool. Brittle grass hisses in the wind, and small blue flowers grow where the stones stay damp.
rooms.1061: The path ends on a small windy terrace overlooking the whole sweep of the valley. A ring of low marble posts, once linked by chains, marks where pilgrims used to rest and pray. Heat shimmers on the stones, and the place feels watched from above. The only way back is south down the stony rise.
rooms.1058: The gully is choked with fallen marble, huge white blocks wedged between the cliff walls like the pieces of a dropped toy. Ferns grow in the damp shade between them. The only path leads back north to the colonnade. Somewhere inside the heap a draught whistles through a hollow.
rooms.1057: A steep track begins at the edge of the domed crossing, with rough steps cut into the living rock. It climbs north up the slope, while the pillared roof lies back to the east. Wild rosemary spills over the edges of the steps. Scorch marks on the rock tell of lightning strikes that fell here long ago.
rooms.1062: The ridge track levels onto a broad bench of rock with a clear view over the pale valley floor. South the track drops back to the pillared crossing, and west it goes on through a notch in the stone. Gnarled junipers grow from the cracks, twisted by the winds. A cairn of white stones stands at the edge, built by some forgotten traveller.
rooms.1063: The track forks in a bowl of tumbled rock, with a flat boulder carved with a fading spiral in the middle of the junction. A gentler path runs on north, a rough way winds down to the south, and the bench above the valley lies back east. The air here is cooler and smells of wet stone and sage.
rooms.1064: A narrow shelf of rock hangs over a long drop, ending at a ledge where the wind is fierce enough to push at your cloak. Far below, the valley floor is a pattern of paler and darker stone, split by the old stream bed. The only way out is the path back south. Lightning flickers in the cloud at eye level, and the hair on your arms rises.
rooms.1065: A cleft in the rock holds a shrine no bigger than a cupboard, its marble god long since carried off or broken. Dry laurel leaves lie heaped in the alcove. The only way back leads north to the fork in the track. Wind whispers in the cleft with something very like a voice.
rooms.1001: The White Marble Stairs climb steeply inside a vaulted shaft, each step as wide as a wagon and polished smooth by countless feet. Pale light seeps from somewhere overhead, and the walls sweat with a cool mist. Looking back down the flight you can still see the landing, small and bright.
rooms.1002: Halfway into the climb the steps grow cold and the air thins. Carved laurel wreaths run along the walls, each leaf cut so finely that it seems to stir in the draught. The marble underfoot is veined with grey, like clouds trapped in stone.
rooms.1003: The stair narrows here, and slits in the wall let in the roar of wind from outside. Each step is chipped at the edge, as if some huge weight once climbed it in haste. A smell of rain and hot metal drifts down from above. The steps seem endless, yet the light ahead grows steadily brighter.
rooms.1004: The stairs end at a wide landing beneath a doorway of gold-veined stone, its heavy lintel carved with a spiral of winding paths. Beyond the arch the air feels dry and charged, as before a storm. The last steps are worn nearly flat. Muffled thunder comes from within, as steady as a heartbeat.
rooms.1005: The Labyrinth begins as a low hall of white marble, cut by narrow turnings that seem to double back on themselves. A mosaic spiral covers the floor, its tesserae gold and bone. Cold lamplight burns without flame in niches along the walls. The air is dry and still, and your footsteps return from places they should not reach.
rooms.1006: Walls of marble streaked with black rise to a ceiling lost in gloom, and every passage ends in another identical archway. Bronze rings hang from the stonework at head height, rusted shut. Scratches at the foot of one wall form a tally of days kept by someone long gone. A faint draught smells of oil and old blood.
rooms.1007: A round chamber opens off the winding ways, its domed ceiling painted with stars that have mostly flaked away. In the centre stands a dry basin of green marble, cracked and empty. Six archways ring the room, and each looks exactly like the others. The silence is thick enough to press on the ears.
rooms.1008: The passage is so narrow here that your shoulders brush the cold walls. Carved friezes run along both sides, showing a bull-headed figure hunted through a maze by heroes with bronze spears. The carvings are chipped at the faces, as though someone hated what they showed. Water drips somewhere ahead with a slow, patient rhythm.
rooms.1009: Broken columns lie across the floor of this hall like felled trees, forcing a crooked path through the rubble. The ceiling has fallen in places, and heaps of white dust glitter on the tiles. Great cloven hoofprints are pressed into the dust, then scuffed half away. A smell of musk and wet straw lingers in the stale air.
rooms.1010: A long gallery lined with mirrors of polished silver stretches ahead, each sheet warped and clouded with tarnish. Your reflection stretches and bends as you pass, sometimes with one arm too many. The floor is laid in black and white squares like a game board. A sweet, heavy scent of incense hangs in the air.
rooms.1011: This hall is a dead row of sealed doors, dozens of them set into the marble, each with a bronze handle shaped like a lion's head. None opens when tried, and the corridor between them twists on. Torches in iron brackets have burned down to black stubs. Cold air creeps from the cracks around the doors.
rooms.1012: The floor tilts gently here, and the walls curve with it, giving the odd sense of walking round the inside of a giant shell. Seashells set into the marble in neat spirals glitter in the dim light. A green stain of sea-damp runs down the stone, though no sea lies within a hundred leagues. Distant thunder shakes loose a thin rain of dust.
rooms.1013: Statues of tired heroes line this hall, each carved with an expression of despair, as if they too had lost their way. Their stone hands are held out palms upward, and some have been snapped off at the wrist. A thread of gold wire, long tangled and dull, still trails across the floor. A sound like slow breathing seems to come from the walls.
rooms.1014: This last coil of the Labyrinth ends at a tall arch of white marble framing a bright street beyond. The walls are smoother here, their carving fresh and sharp, and the air smells of open sky. A path of pale flagstones leads north out of the maze. Behind you the passages turn dark and secretive again.
rooms.1015: A broad avenue of polished white marble leaves the mouth of the Labyrinth, shining like a frozen river under the storm light. To the south the arched maze entrance opens in a wall of stone, and to the north the street runs on toward a plaza. Slender pillars topped with carved garlands flank the avenue. Thunder rolls over the rooftops, and the scent of ambrosia hangs in the wind.
rooms.1016: The street meets a quiet plaza where a dry fountain stands, its marble dolphins worn to blank stumps. To the west a low doorway of green stone leads into a demigod's abode, while the avenue runs east between empty colonnades and south back toward the maze. Gilded weather vanes creak on the rooftops. Olive leaves drift across the paving.
rooms.1019: The street bends between tall white walls inlaid with bands of lapis blue. Statues of stern heroes stand in wall niches, most of them missing hands or heads. The street runs north toward a wider square and west back toward the plaza. A warm wind carries the smell of laurel smoke.
rooms.1020: A wide square lies before the great cathedral, ringed with cypresses in marble planters. A white house carved with feathers stands to the west, a demigod's abode opens to the east, and the street runs south, while the cathedral's golden doors rise to the north. The paving is inlaid with a pattern of rays, like a sun carved into the stone. Lightning glints off the high gilded roofs.
rooms.1023: The doorway of the Gods' Cathedral is a deep arch lined with rows of carved winged figures, their faces turned toward the street. Inside the entrance a vestibule of cool marble lies hushed beneath a high vaulted roof. Bronze lamps hang from chains, all long unlit. The way south leads back to the square, and the nave opens to the north.
rooms.1024: The nave of the Gods' Cathedral is vast, a hall of pillars so tall that their capitals vanish in a haze of cloud-coloured light. Rows of empty benches face a great flight of white steps. At the top of the steps the Gods' Table spreads like a stone plateau, bare and silent. The vestibule lies south of here, and the echoes of your own steps return like distant applause.
rooms.1025: You stand atop the Gods' Table itself, a slab of white marble as broad as a meadow and open to a thunder-filled sky. Here the Olympians once feasted, and the places along its rim are still marked by carved cups the size of cauldrons. Steps lead down into the cathedral below, and a winged throne stands to the east. The wind smells of ambrosia and scorched air.
rooms.1026: The throne of Hermes is a light seat of white marble, its arms carved like wings swept back for flight. Stone sandals are set into the plinth at its foot. The Table stretches west toward the great stairs, and a path runs north along its rim toward another throne. Wind tugs at your clothes, and lightning flashes along the horizon.
rooms.1027: Apollo's throne is a high seat of white marble fronted by a great sunburst of beaten gold, dulled now by weather. The strings of a lyre are carved along the armrests, one of them cracked clean through. The path leads back south to the throne of Hermes and west along the Table into a roofed stretch. The light has a warm, honeyed quality here, even beneath the storm.
rooms.1028: A roofed stretch of the Gods' Table passes through a gallery of rose-coloured columns, its ceiling painted with pale doves. The table runs on west toward a throne of pink stone. Carved bowls line its surface, each rimmed with dried gold. The air is warm, perfumed and strangely close.
rooms.1029: Aphrodite's throne is a shell of pink-veined marble, its curved back carved with roses and doves. Stone petals lie scattered in drifts around the seat. The table turns north toward another throne. A heady fragrance of rose and myrrh clings to the stone, sweet beneath the sharper tang of ozone.
rooms.1030: Artemis's throne is a seat of pale silver-white stone, its back shaped like a crescent moon. A frieze of running hounds and arrows wraps the plinth. The table runs east from here along a line of low pillars. A cold, clean wind sighs among the pillars, smelling of pine and rain.
rooms.1031: The Gods' Table narrows here to a stately ribbon of marble, wide enough for six to walk abreast. Its surface is scored with the long-dried stains of spilled wine. The way runs east toward a throne draped in carved ivy. Thunder cracks overhead, and a few fat drops of rain strike the stone.
rooms.1032: Dionysus's throne is a tangle of carved vines in dark green marble, with grapes the size of fists hanging from its arms. Wine-dark stains seep into the plinth and never quite dry. The table turns north from this seat. The air smells of crushed grapes and the sweet sourness of ancient feasts.
rooms.1033: Hephaestus's throne is forged rather than carved, a seat of black iron and bronze set into the marble with a great anvil for its back. Soot stains the stone around it, and a rack of stone tongs and hammers is fixed to the plinth. The table runs west into a roofed gallery. A faint warmth rises from the metal, as if a forge still burned somewhere beneath.
rooms.1034: Here the Gods' Table passes inside a pillared hall of grey-veined stone, its ceiling hung with carved owls and olive branches. Marble cups the size of buckets line the board. The table leads west toward a throne of pale stone. The hall is cool and quiet, and the thunder is only a murmur.
rooms.1035: Before Athena's throne stands a tall, helm-crowned seat of white marble, its back wrought in the shape of a great shield. A carved owl perches on the headrest, its eyes of dull glass staring. Spears and scrolls are cut into the plinth in careful order. The table turns north from here, and the room smells of wax, ink and old bronze.
rooms.1036: Demeter's throne is woven from carved wheat in golden stone, with sheaves bending along the backrest. Dry husks and petals lie in drifts across the floor, though nothing grows here. The table runs east from the seat. The air is thick with the ghost of warm bread and dry earth.
rooms.1037: A low arcade lined with iron torch-brackets crosses this stretch of the table, its floor scuffed by heavy boots. Spear racks of marble stand against the wall, empty. The table runs east toward a seat of dark red stone. A metallic smell hangs in the air, and the stone feels oddly warm.
rooms.1038: Ares' throne is a brutal seat of red-black stone, its arms carved as clenched fists and its back set with a hundred stone spearheads. Great gouges mark the floor, as if blades had been dragged across it in anger. The table turns north from here. A smell of iron and sweat lingers, and the silence seems to wait for a fight.
rooms.1039: Poseidon's throne rises like a wave frozen at its crest, carved from blue-green marble with a trident-shaped crack through its back. The floor around it is damp, though no water seeps in. The table runs west toward the head of the feast. Briny air, sea-cold and sharp, hangs in the hall.
rooms.1040: The Gods' Table ends in a wide hall at its head, where the greatest seats face the length of the feast. A broad arch leads north to the throne of the king of the gods, and a smaller one opens west to his queen's seat. The ceiling is lost in shadow, and the floor is inlaid with a pattern of lightning in gold. Every footstep rings.
rooms.1042: Zeus's mighty throne towers over the hall, a seat of white marble twice the height of a man, its arms carved as eagles' wings. Blackened scars run across the steps where lightning once struck and gathered. A narrow doorway of dark stone opens north behind the seat into a place of old silence. The air tingles, and the hairs on your neck rise.

1043.description: The tomb is a low vault of black stone, cold as a winter well, where the titan lord was bound after the war. Great chains as thick as a man's body run from the walls to a ring set in the floor. The air smells of damp earth and iron, and a slow pulse seems to beat in the rock. Faded runes cover the walls in rings, each one cut deeper than the last.

rooms.1041: Hera's throne is a seat of ivory-white marble crowned with a carved diadem of peacock feathers. Fine drapes of stone fall from its canopy, cut with such skill that they seem to move. The only way out is back east to the head of the Table. The room is cold and formal, and the faint scent of lilies lingers.
rooms.1021: This demigod's abode is a spacious hall of cream-coloured stone with a cracked marble hearth, a curved couch carved from a single block and wall niches empty of trophies. Faded frescoes of hunts and games cover the walls. The doorway opens west onto the square. A fine layer of dust lies on everything, and the room smells of cold ash.
rooms.1022: The angel's house is a small round chamber of luminous white stone, its domed ceiling carved with slender feathers that overlap like a wing. A bare perch is set into the wall beside a basin of clear stone. The door opens east to the square. Everything is hushed, and the light seems to come from the stone itself.
rooms.1018: This demigod's lodging is a low, dim hall of green-black stone, its walls hung with the rotted remnants of tapestries. A great round shield of bronze, dented and green, is fixed above the fireplace. A broad bed of stone stands along one wall with a pillow carved of marble. The only way out leads east to the plaza. The air is stale and chilly.
rooms.1099: A hidden chamber stands apart from the winding ways, its walls thick with soot and its floor strewn with shards of broken pottery. A great altar of black stone fills one end, grooved with channels for offerings. Faded paintings on the wall show a king feeding youths into the maze. The air is heavy with the cold of a place where hope was lost.

1044.description: Two marble pillars stand at the valley mouth, joined by a lintel carved with a procession of robed figures. Frost has split the lintel, and the figures have lost their faces.

1052.description: The plinth is a block of white marble taller than a man. Only a pair of carved stone feet remains on top, as if the god it held simply stepped away.

1050.description: Each milestone carries a column of letters in an ancient script, rubbed nearly smooth by wind. A few still show a single repeated sign, a bolt of lightning.

1065.description: The alcove is empty but for a worn footprint in the stone where the god's statue once stood. Someone has left fresh-looking laurel leaves in a ring around it.

1016.description: The fountain basin is bone dry, and the four marble dolphins at its centre have been worn by wind and rain until they look like sleeping fists.

1025.description: The carved cups along the rim of the Table are each large enough to bathe in. Deep inside every one lies a faint gold stain, the last of the nectar.

1043.description: The chains are forged from a dull grey metal that sheds frost when touched. The runes spiral inward toward the ring, repeating a single word of binding.

1042.description: The scars on the steps are fused glass, black and glossy, shaped like branching rivers. They are still faintly warm.

creatures.long_desc: A bronze-clawed harpy circles overhead, shrieking and eyeing you hungrily.
creatures.description: She has the body of a vulture and the withered face of an old woman, with talons that glint like new bronze. Her feathers are stained with soot and the gold dust of the empty high places.

creatures.long_desc: A golden-maned lion paces the stones, its hide shimmering like beaten metal.
creatures.description: A lion of the old mountain kind, huge and tawny, its mane shining as though dusted with gold. Its claws leave grooves in the white stone as it walks.

creatures.long_desc: A living marble guard stands rigid at its post, spear leveled at the unwary.
creatures.description: A towering warrior carved of white stone, with blank eyes and a hoplite's crest. It moves with a grinding slowness, but each swing of its spear lands like a falling column.

creatures.long_desc: A snorting minotaur stalks the passages, its horns scraping the marble walls.
creatures.description: A hulking man with the head of a bull, slick with sweat and wild with rage. Its horns are chipped from a thousand blows against stone, and its breath steams in the cold.

creatures.long_desc: A storm chimera prowls the white streets, a snake-tail lashing behind it.
creatures.description: A beast of three bodies, with a lion's head, a goat's head along its spine and a serpent for a tail. Sparks crackle along its mane, and it smells of burnt hair.

creatures.long_desc: A snake-haired gorgon lurks in the dim passages, her hissing locks writhing.
creatures.description: A lean, scaled woman whose hair is a mass of living snakes. Fragments of statues lie in the dust around her feet, still frozen in the shape of fear.

creatures.short_desc: Talos, Bronze Guardian of the Thrones
creatures.long_desc: Talos, Bronze Guardian of the Thrones, stands in the arch, his bronze limbs glowing with inner heat.
creatures.description: A giant of living bronze, his single vein running with molten gold behind a nail at his ankle. He turns his helmed head slowly toward you, and the whole hall rings with each step he takes.
rooms: At the Head of The Gods' Table

creatures.long_desc: Hyperion, the Chained Titan, strains against his bonds, his eyes blazing like twin suns.
creatures.description: A titan of the elder race, so tall that his head brushes the vault of the tomb. Great chains bind his limbs, yet he drags against them, and the stone trembles with every pull.
rooms: The Tomb of Kronos, Lord of the Titans

items.room_desc: A cloak of dark harpy feathers lies here.
items.description: Dark, glossy feathers are sewn in overlapping rows onto a light grey cloth. It rustles in even a faint breeze.

items.room_desc: A round shield faced with white marble lies here.
items.description: A round bronze shield faced with a thin slab of white marble. A snarling face is carved at its centre.

items.room_desc: A double-bladed bronze labrys lies here.
items.description: A heavy axe with a crescent blade on either side of its haft. Maze patterns are etched along the bronze.

items.room_desc: A pair of bronze greaves lies here, warm to the touch.
items.description: Greaves of golden bronze that stay faintly warm. Fine channels run through the metal like veins.

items.short_desc: the Sundering Maul of the titans
items.room_desc: An enormous stone maul lies here, rimmed with frost.
items.description: A maul with a head of black stone, cold enough to numb the hand, and a haft bound in links of broken chain. It was made for a hand far larger than yours.
